card.situation: NPS NACE FY26 Hazardous Tree Cyclic Maintenance (RFQ 140P3026Q0042): full-spectrum arboricultural services — tree removal, pruning, chipping, meadow restoration, storm response — in the Washington DC area under NAICS 561730, Total Small Business Set-Aside.\nFlagged for owner review because the firm is SB-eligible and holds federal grounds maintenance past performance, but the matrix returned a fit score of 0.3 with two disqualifying gaps: place of performance is 1,000+ miles from Oklahoma City (violates owner distance rule), and no ISA Certified Arborist is on staff despite being a mandatory on-site requirement.
reasons_for: Firm is eligible for the Total Small Business set-aside as a WOSB/EDWOSB/SBA small business, so no eligibility barrier exists [83debc9c-1900ffa2-p1-bea87149].
OSHA 30 supervisors, QC/CMMS program, and occupied-federal-facility experience satisfy general worksite safety and orderliness requirements [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p6-088b3de4].
Federal grounds maintenance past performance at Tinker AFB demonstrates scheduling, advance-notice coordination, and federal invoicing familiarity [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p2-aa340b0c].
reasons_against: Place of performance is National Capital Parks-East (Washington DC area), well over 200 miles from Oklahoma City, triggering the owner's hard distance rule [rc-distance].

No ISA Certified Arborist is listed anywhere in the firm profile, yet one must be on-site at all times and a certification ID provided before work begins — a disqualifying gap [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p5-1d4fbf28].

No tree climbing crew, hazardous tree removal capability, 12-inch chipper, log-moving machine, or chip truck is listed in the profile, leaving the core equipment and labor scope entirely unmet [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p2-ec258b3e].

drafts.capability_statement:
Red Cedar Facility Services is a Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), and SBA-certified small business operating under NAICS 561730, the exact code cited in RFQ 140P3026Q0042. We are fully eligible for this Total Small Business Set-Aside.

Red Cedar brings federal grounds and vegetation management experience from occupied installations including a GSA-managed federal building in Oklahoma City, a VA outpatient clinic, and cantonment area grounds maintenance at Tinker AFB — all performed under firm-fixed-price contracts with federal quality and safety standards. Our workforce of 38 W-2 employees is supervised by OSHA 30-certified leads, and all work is tracked through a CMMS that logs QC inspections and supports federal submittal schedules.

Our safety culture is built on OSHA compliance, PPE enforcement, and a documented green cleaning and grounds program. We hold CIMS-GB certification and maintain e-Verify enrollment. We have demonstrated the ability to work in occupied federal facilities with minimal disruption, coordinate advance scheduling with government technical representatives, and meet federal invoicing and payment requirements.

We understand the NPS NACE scope requires full-spectrum arboricultural services including hazardous tree removal, pruning, chipping, and meadow restoration in accordance with ANSI Z-133, ANSI A300, and ISA best management practices. We are prepared to address our technical approach, crew composition, equipment plan, and past performance in the three-volume format specified in the solicitation.
questions_for_co: ISA Certified Arborist requirement [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p5-1d4fbf28 / p2-01c70090 / p5-21efd13d]: The solicitation requires an ISA Certified Arborist on-site at all times. Will the Government accept a teaming arrangement or subcontract with a local ISA-certified arborist to satisfy this requirement, or must the arborist be a direct W-2 employee of the prime contractor?

Crew and equipment sourcing [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p2-5cfb9cbc / p2-ec258b3e / p3-624f9e4e]: The solicitation requires a minimum five-person crew including two climbers, a 12-inch-capacity chipper, a log-moving machine, and a chip truck. May a prime contractor satisfy these requirements through a subcontractor or equipment rental arrangement, provided all personnel and equipment are on-site and available for each scheduled work day?

Arboricultural licenses and permits [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p4-2ff902a6]: What specific arboricultural licenses or permits does the Government anticipate will be required for performance within NACE boundaries, and are any of those permits obtained by or through the National Park Service rather than the contractor?

Insurance and liability coverage levels [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p4-481e09bf]: The solicitation references full contractor liability for loss or damage to Government property and third-party claims. What minimum general liability and workers' compensation insurance coverage amounts are required, and will those be specified in the final contract or an amendment?

Work/treatment log format and DBH reporting [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p8-f5ee1806 / p8-be8e1a74]: Is there a Government-prescribed template or data format for the work/treatment log (specimen, DBH, standard industry terms, tree health/hazard notes), or may the contractor propose its own format for COR approval prior to the first work day?

Traffic control and MUTCD lane closure scope [83debc9c-6d4d27fc-p3-34cd3fc3 / p3-5b25afad]: How frequently are lane closures on parkways or roads anticipated during a typical cyclic maintenance cycle, and does the Government hold any blanket traffic control permits within NACE that the contractor may operate under, or must the contractor independently obtain all MUTCD-compliant traffic control plans and permits?

reader.scope_summary: The National Park Service (NACE) is procuring hazardous tree cyclic maintenance services requiring a contractor to provide all labor, management, supervision, materials, tools, supplies, transportation, and equipment to perform safe full-spectrum pruning operations in accordance with ANSI Z-133 and ANSI A300 standards and ISA best management practices. Mitigation work includes tree removal, meadow restoration, vegetation removal, tree pruning, chipping, log removal, storm damage response, and creation of clear zones on trails, roads, and parkways within the national park. The contract is a Firm Fixed Price vehicle solicited under RFQ 140P3026Q0042 as a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS 561730.
reader.evaluation_basis: Quotes are evaluated on three volumes: Volume I – Technical Capability, Volume II – Past Performance (three completed questionnaires from references for recent work of same or similar size and scope), and Volume III – Price. The solicitation states "Quotes shall address each evaluation criterion and sub-criterion with particular emphasis on areas of cited specialized work and knowledge," but no explicit weighting or best-value tradeoff methodology is stated beyond these three factors.
